worlds.title: The Water Mark in Rowan Flat
worlds.discipline: Household repair reasoning (a shared-flat leak review)
worlds.public_question: What caused the new water mark on Rowan Flat's kitchen ceiling?

public_rules.plain_language: A fitting released water during the incident when it opens under raised pressure and the building pressure rose during that same interval.
A source that released water during the incident caused the ceiling mark when a direct traced path connects that source to the mark.
A shower caused the mark only if it ran during the incident and water from its screen was traced to the ceiling mark. Timing without a path is not enough.

worlds.title: The Campus FAQ Machine
worlds.discipline: AI Foundations AF1: AI systems, tasks, and agents
worlds.public_question: What should the campus FAQ tool use as its first implementation baseline, on the evidence in the formulation card?

public_rules.plain_language: When the task is a fixed set of intents and an approved answer bank already exists, a deterministic mapping is possible.
If a deterministic mapping is possible and there are no training labels for a learned classifier, the rule-based baseline is sufficient as the first formulation.
Where wrong guidance can affect a student record, retained staff authority matters: the tool may route or display approved guidance, but its output is not the institutional decision.
If the rule baseline is sufficient, model output is not the decision, and wrong advice is an unacceptable failure, the correct first approach is the rule-based baseline.

worlds.title: The Unsigned Nocturne
worlds.public_question: Who composed the unsigned nocturne found in the flooded archive of the Cassia Conservatory?

public_rules.plain_language: A leaf carries its mill's watermark; if a paper stock was in the copy-room only during one period, whatever is written on that stock was written there in that period.
Ink betrays its batch; if a work's ink was mixed only during one period, the work was written in that period.
Whoever was at the conservatory during the period a work was written there could have written it; no one writes in a room they never entered.
The copy-room ledger does not lie: whoever signed it through a period was at the conservatory then.
If a work quotes a tune that was kept within one house's walls — never printed, never performed — then whoever dwelled within those walls had the source of the work.
The archive attributes a work to one who could have written it, who had its source, and whose hand corrected its draft — copyists copy fair; only the composer strikes out and rewrites.

released_evidence.surface: Every musician shown the leaves says the same: this is Vess's late manner — the suspensions, the long pedal, the way the bass walks.
Held to the lamp, every leaf of the nocturne shows the same heron watermark — the Brell mill's mark.

released_evidence.plain_language: stock used only during: heron stock · flood winter
released_evidence.surface: The steward's stock-book is plain: heron paper entered the copy-room in the winter of the flood, and the last of it was spent before the thaw. None before, none since.
The capital's concert bills run unbroken through the flood winter: Vess played the Esten halls every week of it, and did not return until the thaw.

released_evidence.plain_language: at conservatory during: liane · flood winter
released_evidence.surface: The night porter remembers the flood winter well: the copy-room lamps burned past midnight, week upon week, and it was the archive girl, Liane, who kept them burning.
Played through once, the nocturne gives up its middle voice: it carries an older tune entire — a cradle-song, set like a keepsake under the right hand's figures.
